craft_notes: Sthāyin: identity riddles (you-alone/I-alone/both-not). Rows: row 2 (am-not→homage). Close: homage (thrice — the question dissolves into bowing). Rejected: 'only you, only I' smoothing — kept alone-thrice (eva hammered); answering the riddle — kept unanswered (questions ARE the verse).

lines: You, you alone; I, I alone. You alone are; I, nowise.
You and I, both — where is homage, homage, homage?
l4.sanskrit_cite: tvaṃ tvamevāhamevāhaṃ tvamevāsi na cāsmyaham | ahaṃ tvamityubhau na sto yatra tasmai namo namaḥ

reads_against.argmap: Who are you, who am I? → Identity and non-identity both refused: neither you alone nor I alone, nor both — only homage where the question lands.
c1_essence: You alone, I alone; you are, I am not; both are not — only homage.
